ava: weird in ap-northeast1: several small GPU helpers are repeatedly evicted while GPUs show as free in the allocator.

nate: any recent drains or node kubelet restarts?

ava: yes, automated kernel patch rollout hit rack-3 around 03:10Z and nodes were cordoned then uncordoned quickly. we see batches of pods moved and tiny helpers getting preempted.

deploy-bot: rollout/kernel-upgrade v1.8.4 started by @nate at 2026-06-11T03:08Z

nate: looks like our drain concurrency default (concurrency=10) plus scheduler's rack-spread policy causes adjacent racks to pick up workloads and then preempt low-priority helpers to make room. that leaves isolated free GPUs inside racks (fragmentation).

ava: logs: ```
I0611 03:11:05 drain.go:112 cordon node=apn3-rack3-n04
I0611 03:11:09 drain.go:130 evict pod=helper-slim-21 node=apn3-rack3-n04
I0611 03:11:12 scheduler.go:401 preempt pod=helper-slim-22 target=node=apn3-rack4-n02
```

ops-oncall: impact: spike in preemptRate for small system pods, fragmentedGpuCount on rack3 rose to 6, scheduling latency up ~1.8s for tiny pods. overall GPU utilization steady.

nate: mitigation: 1) reduce drain concurrency to 3 for kernel patch rollouts in GPU racks, 2) enable preempt-jitter to spread evictions, 3) exclude system-helper pods from immediate preempt for 120s after a node uncordon.

ava: temporary config changes applied to ap-northeast1 patch job. watching.

ops-oncall: alert created infra-7560. please add cost note if churn visible.

nate: followups: metric to add: fragmentedGpuCount_by_rack, drainConcurrencyHistogram, preemptWaveSize. also add a canary rule: if fragmentedGpuCount>5 for >10m, pause any rolling drains in region.

deploy-bot: kernel-upgrade v1.8.4 completed for ap-northeast1-rack3 at 2026-06-11T03:45Z

ops-oncall: alert cleared: ap-northeast1 helper-preempt-wave 1m duration. monitoring remains on. thanks :thumbsup:
